1500.body:
## What this fixes

The rail paints `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` at 32x32 on a `#f5f5f5` surface. Since `6614a0c4` ("switch logo, app mark and Windows icon to the rounded light variant") that PNG fills its whole 128x128 canvas with a white rounded square - 93.6% of its pixels are fully opaque and 60.3% are pure white - so the rail shows a white tile with the mark inside it instead of the mark itself.

This replaces the asset with the transparent cut of the official light artwork, corrects the stylesheet comment that described a tile, and gives the shell's first-run pages the same cut so one launch does not change the mark halfway through. Three files: the PNG, `design.css` (comment), `application/scripts/build.mjs` (the copy source).

## How the asset was made

- Source: the official vertical light logo, rendered at 8x on a transparent page.
- The wordmark is everything below the fully transparent band at y=471-564 of that render; the mark above it is 320x372 px there.
- Crop: a square canvas sized on the mark's long side (394 px at 8x, ~6% above and below), resized to 128x128 with Lanczos, RGBA.
- Measured on the file that ships, with explicit thresholds: ink box (`alpha > 0`) 109x126 px inside 128, margins 10 px left, 9 px right, 1 px above and below; `alpha = 255` on 29.6% of the canvas, `alpha = 0` on 55.1%, and the remaining 15.3% partial. At `background-size: 32px` that draws the mark at about 27x31.5 px - it is a tall mark, so it fills the box vertically and keeps its air on the sides.
- The file keeps the 128 px size the stylesheet asks for, so `background-size: 32px 32px` and `border-radius: 8px` are untouched.

## Where the mark is painted

Six surfaces paint it, all on a light background:

| surface | rule / file | background |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rail | `apps/desktop/src/styles/design.css:90` | `#f5f5f5` (`.rail`) |
| sign-in page header | `apps/desktop/src/styles/login.css:36` | `#fff` (`.login-page`) |
| setup-wizard header | `apps/desktop/src/styles/wizard.css:59` | `#fff` (`.wizard-page`) |
| 技能 › 从 GitHub 导入 | `apps/desktop/src/styles/settings.css:1807` | `#fff` (settings dialog) |
| shell loading page | `application/src/loading.html` (`.wizard-brand-mark`) | `#fff` |
| shell first-run page | `application/src/wizard.html` (same rule) | `#fff` |

The last two load `app-mark.png` from `dist/`, which `application/scripts/build.mjs` writes - now from the renderer's asset, so they paint this file too.

The remaining three mentions do not paint anything themselves: `apps/desktop/src/views/Rail.tsx:76` and `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/SkillGitImportView.tsx:259` name it in a comment and a class name, and `application/scripts/build.mjs` is the copy step.

## The shell pages paint the same cut

Before this branch `build.mjs` copied `application/build/icon-256.png` to `dist/app-mark.png`, so the pages that load before React painted the old tile at 24x26 px inside the 32 px box while the rail painted 28x30 px - the mark changed as the loading page handed over to the SPA.

The fix is not to make `icon-256.png` transparent. That one file has three jobs:

- `dist/icon.png` - the tray image (`application/src/main.ts:1601`), which sits on unknown desktop backgrounds and needs its tile;
- the OLD source of `dist/app-mark.png`, the shell brand row, until this branch;
- the 256 frame `application/scripts/make-icon.ps1` wraps into `build/icon.ico` for the installer and taskbar.

So `build.mjs` now copies the renderer's transparent asset to `dist/app-mark.png` and leaves `dist/icon.png` exactly where it was: the UI gets the transparent cut, the system icons keep the opaque one.

Verified by running those two copy statements as written (same `join`/`cpSync` expressions) in the shell package: `dist/app-mark.png` comes out byte-identical to `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png` (md5 `9263f9c9...`) and `dist/icon.png` byte-identical to `build/icon-256.png` (md5 `5081a365...`), so the tray image did not move. `node --check application/scripts/build.mjs` exits 0. The whole script could not be run here - the shell package's `node_modules` are not installed in this checkout and esbuild stops on `electron-updater` - so the esbuild half was not executed; the copy half is what this diff changes, and that is what I ran.

## Frames

Pinned to commit `97142e04` on `yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery:screenshots-appmark`, not to a branch name. Harness: `apps/desktop/e2e` - Vite on its own port, `fixtures.ts` answers every `/api/**` request; viewport 1280x820, DPR 1, zh-CN. The only difference between a "before" and its "after" is `app-mark.png`.

![rail mark, before and after, 2x](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-after-rail-2x.png)

| frame | what it shows |
| --- | --- |
| [before-rail-160.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-rail-160.png) | the rail's top-left corner as shipped: white rounded tile, 32 px |
| [after-rail-160.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/after-rail-160.png) | the same corner with this head: the mark on `#f5f5f5`, no tile |
| [before-window-1280.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-window-1280.png) | the whole 1280x820 window before |
| [after-window-1280.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/after-window-1280.png) | the whole 1280x820 window after |
| [before-login-brand.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/before-login-brand.png) | the sign-in header at 32 px on `#fff`, before |
| [after-login-brand.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/97142e048087cce977f891581cc6c9f029f93c21/shots/app-mark/after-login-brand.png) | the same header after: on white the tile was invisible already, so only the mark itself differs |

**Frames for the two shell pages.** `application/src/loading.html` and `application/src/wizard.html` are plain HTML with inline CSS, so both were rendered directly at `e969931e`: the shipped markup and stylesheet, the same 1440x900 viewport at DPR 2, and only `app-mark.png` swapped between the two copies (`application/build/icon-256.png`, md5 `5081a365…`, which is what the old `build.mjs` copied, versus `apps/desktop/src/assets/brand/app-mark.png`, md5 `9263f9c9…`). `wizard.html` replaces its body when `window.sdShell.wizard` is absent, so its preload bridge was stubbed; no markup, style or asset was altered, and the loading page needed no stub because its bridge calls are guarded.

| page | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| loading (full / brand row) | [full](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/before-shell-loading-full.png) · [brand](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/before-shell-loading-brand.png) | [full](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/after-shell-loading-full.png) · [brand](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/after-shell-loading-brand.png) |
| first run (full / brand row) | [full](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/before-shell-wizard-full.png) · [brand](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/before-shell-wizard-brand.png) | [full](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/after-shell-wizard-full.png) · [brand](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/7a56e7141966dd9054fe4dc910899a06b79c7e0c/shots/app-mark/after-shell-wizard-brand.png) |

Measured on those pages at the 32 px draw size: the old copy paints the mark at 22.25x25.75 px inside a 32x32 white tile (93.9 % of it fully opaque), the new one at 27.25x31.5 px with no tile (29.6 % fully opaque, 55.1 % fully transparent, ink margins 2.5 / 2.25 / 0.25 / 0.25 px) - the size step earlier frames could only show on the rail. Those ink boxes use a `r/g/b < 245` threshold; the 24x26 and 28x30 figures used earlier come from a looser one, and both agree in direction and ratio (about 1.22x on each axis).

**Two of the six surfaces still have no frame**, and neither is claimed to look right:

- The setup-wizard header inside the renderer. Its only harness, `apps/desktop/src/wizard-shot.dev.tsx`, exports `mountWizardShotHarness` and documents a `?wizard-shot=1` entry, but nothing in `main.tsx` references it, so that entry is dead; without an account session the app falls back to the sign-in page. Capturing it needs an account session or a temporary entry point in someone else's tree, which is beyond this change.
- The skill-import dialog. It is rendered by `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/SkillsSettings.tsx:1002` (`SkillGitImportView`), no spec under `apps/desktop/e2e` mentions it, and it did not open from the skills pane under these mocks; why it fails there has not been established, so no reason is claimed for it.

The sign-in header pair stands in for the 32 px / `#fff` rule both of them follow, not as a photograph of either.

`raw.githubusercontent.com` did not answer from this machine while I was writing this, so each file was checked through the contents API at that commit instead: every remote size equals the local byte count exactly.

## Not changed on purpose

- `docs/images/logo.png` and the installer icons (`application/build/icon-256.png`, `icon.ico`, `icon.icns`) keep their tile: an OS icon is shown against unknown desktop backgrounds, and a transparent one would disappear on a dark taskbar. Switching those to the new artwork is a separate change, not this one.
- `border-radius: 8px` on `.rail-logo` stays: it has no visible effect on a transparent asset and keeps the rule correct if a filled asset is ever used again.

## Testing

- No runtime logic changed: one binary asset, one CSS comment, and one copy source in `application/scripts/build.mjs`. It does change what two shell pages paint - they now draw the same cut at the same size as the rail, where they drew 24x26 px before.
- No unit test asserts the pixels of the mark and I did not add one - a jsdom test cannot read the PNG's alpha without a decoder dependency, and the frames above are what a person can actually check.
- `L1`, `UT` and `ST` do not read this asset, and the CSS edit is inside a comment; the shell copy is exercised by the `application` build in the packaging job, not by those suites.

1501.author: qingkwl
1501.body:
## Problem

osx-sign's `isbinaryfile` probe misjudges ~2500 pure DATA files as Mach-O (NUL bytes in the first 8000) and walks them into the per-file `codesign --timestamp` loop. Two signed builds (2026-11-25, m5 tree) both died mid-marathon with:

```
A timestamp was expected but was not found
```

The ~2h / ~2500-roundtrip timestamp load trips Apple's TSA rate limit, killing the whole `SD_MAC_SIGN=1` release build.

## Change

Extend `mac.signIgnore` (electron-builder.yml) with 13 patterns covering the misjudged cohorts. Cohorts were verified by scanning the actual release bundle (92376 files):

| Cohort | Pattern(s) | ~Files |
|---|---|---|
| timezone blobs | `zoneinfo/` | 598 + ~500 (tzdata/pytz) |
| PDF CMap tables | `/cmap/` | ~212 + 148 (`*.json.gz`) |
| numpy/scipy/sklearn test data | `/tests?/data/`, `/datasets/(data|images)/`, `.npz`, `.mat`, `.sav`, `.wav`, `.fits` | ~560 |
| fonts / static libs / misc | `reportlab/fonts/`, `.a`, `.pfb`, `/babel/locale-data/`, `/mpl-data/` | ~60 |

## Why this is safe

- Skipped files stay in the bundle and remain covered by the **CodeResources seal hashes** — notarization and Gatekeeper are unaffected (same treatment as the existing `.pyc` entry, same story as `.kext` upstream).
- Pattern set validated over the whole bundle: **2555 files matched, 0 true Mach-O harmed** (`.so` 259 / `.dylib` 23 / `bin/python` 2 all still signed).

## Verification

End-to-end proof on this tree (main @ `9e91f78b` + this patch), `SD_MAC_SIGN=1 bash scripts/build-mac.sh`:

- codesign verify OK (Developer ID + hardened runtime, identity match)
- signing completed in ~40 min, **no TSA throttling** (previously died at ~2h)
- `.app` notarized + staple validated; DMG notarized (Submission `91305035-b615-468f-8f15-7eed4ab19e2f`, Accepted) + staple validated
- `spctl -a -vv` accepted for both DMG and `.app` (source=Notarized Developer ID)

Ad-hoc smoke builds (the default, no `SD_MAC_SIGN`) are unaffected — `signIgnore` only feeds the signing path.
1501.head: fix/w23a-signignore-data-files
1501.title: fix(mac-signing): exempt pure data files from per-file codesign timestamping (W23a)

1504.author: yuanzhou75
1504.body:
Closes #1502.

Hint text across the settings panel, the session flyout and the document tabs was drawn below WCAG AA: `.settings-field-hint` at 3.95:1 on the panel, `.settings-ability-option-hint` at 3.95:1 on white and 3.71:1 on the selected option's `#f4f8ff`, `.session-flyout-desc` at 3.36:1 and 3.08:1 on a hovered row, `.session-flyout-note` and `.expert-note` at 3.36:1, `.doc-tab-hint` — the folder that tells two same-named documents apart — at 2.43:1, and the two field counters plus the capability divider at 2.43:1. All of it is 11–12.5 px normal-weight text, so WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 applies at 4.5:1; none of it is an icon, a placeholder or a disabled control.

## What changed

- `tokens.css` gains `--text-hint: #666666`, the value already agreed for the desktop's sidebar hints in #1486 — one secondary colour for hints rather than a fourth shade. `--muted`, `--muted-light` and `--text-faint` keep their values and their call sites: roughly 250 of them, several not text at all, so lifting those would repaint the shell to fix these rules.
- **Nine** rules now name `var(--text-hint)` and nothing else — no per-surface override, no literal left behind: `.settings-field-hint`, `.settings-ability-option-hint`, `.settings-field-count`, `.settings-textarea-count`, `.settings-ability-divider`, `.session-flyout-desc`, `.session-flyout-note`, `.expert-note`, `.doc-tab-hint`.

## One correction to the report, with the evidence

`.doc-tab-hint` is measured in #1502 at **2.14:1** on `--surface-sunk #f0f0f0`, described as "the workspace panel". The panel a reader sees is white: three sheets name `.workspace-panel` — `workspace.css:18` paints it `var(--surface-sunk)`, `workspace.css:169` paints it `var(--surface)`, and `design.css:2495` paints it `#fff` — and `index.css` imports `design.css` **after** `workspace.css`, so the winning declaration is the white one. The folder line is therefore **2.43:1**, not 2.14:1: far below the floor either way, so the defect stands, but the record should carry the number a reader actually meets.

The darker surface is still held **defensively**: the test measures the rule on `--surface-sunk` as well, so the value keeps clearing AA if those later declarations ever go away.

## The frames

All four pairs are real runs of the desktop harness (mocked control plane, no service), rendered at 2× so an 11–12.5 px line is legible. The settings frame is the 专家 form's capability block, which holds both settings hints: the one under the field and the one inside the default-selected full-access option.

| surface | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| capability block: field hint 12.5 px, option hint 12 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-settings.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-settings.png) |
| field counters `0 / 80`, `0 / 500`, 12 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-counters.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-counters.png) |
| flyout description, 12 px, row hovered | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-flyout.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-flyout.png) |
| document tab folder line, 11 px | ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/before-doctab.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/eb39028f8fac04a319294b2375cdcbf23812e55a/docs/screenshots/1502/after-doctab.png) |

Each frame was taken in the same run as a `getComputedStyle` read of the element it shows:

| hint | before | after | surface behind it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.settings-field-hint` | `rgb(128, 128, 128)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `.settings-ability-option-hint` | `rgb(128, 128, 128)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(244, 248, 255)` = `--primary-softer` |
| `.settings-field-count` | `rgb(166, 166, 166)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `.session-flyout-desc` | `rgb(140, 140, 140)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |
| `.doc-tab-hint` | `rgb(166, 166, 166)` | `rgb(102, 102, 102)` | `rgb(255, 255, 255)` |

## Verification

`apps/desktop/tests/hint-contrast-surfaces.test.ts` — seven cases. It reads the sheets, resolves `--text-hint` through `tokens.css`, and asserts 4.5:1 for **each surface a rule is actually painted on**:

```
.settings-field-hint #666666 on settings #ffffff        = 5.74:1
.settings-ability-option-hint #666666 on settings        = 5.74:1
.settings-ability-option-hint #666666 on selectedOption  = 5.39:1
.settings-field-count #666666 on settings                = 5.74:1
.settings-textarea-count #666666 on settings             = 5.74:1
.settings-ability-divider #666666 on settings            = 5.74:1
.session-flyout-desc #666666 on flyout #ffffff           = 5.74:1
.session-flyout-desc #666666 on flyoutHover #f5f5f5      = 5.27:1
.session-flyout-note #666666 on flyout #ffffff           = 5.74:1
.expert-note        #666666 on flyout #ffffff            = 5.74:1
.doc-tab-hint       #666666 on panel #ffffff             = 5.74:1
.doc-tab-hint       #666666 on sunk #f0f0f0              = 5.04:1
```

Beyond the ratios it asserts: each rule declares exactly one colour and names the token; no other rule repaints a hint (only the documented `.settings-field-hint.is-error`, which stays `--danger`); the surfaces it measures are the ones the sheets paint (including the `index.css` load order that decides the panel colour); and the shared muted tokens keep their values.

The pairing itself is asserted, not assumed: the hint inside `.settings-ability-option` is `.settings-ability-option-hint`, so one case reads `SpecialistForm.tsx`, takes the capability option's `<label>…</label>` slice and requires the option's own hint to be inside it, `.settings-field-hint` **not** to be, and the label to carry `is-selected`. That is the mistake this suite had before: it measured `.settings-field-hint` against `#f4f8ff`, a surface that rule never touches.

Mutation runs, each making the test red:

- `.settings-ability-option-hint` back to `#808080` → **3 failed**;
- the option rendering its hint with the `settings-field-hint` class instead (the old wrong pairing, in the DOM) → **1 failed**: `the hint paired with the selected option is the one rendered inside it`;
- `.doc-tab-hint` back to `#a6a6a6` → **3 failed**;
- `--text-hint: #767676`, a grey that clears white at 4.54:1 and nothing else → **2 failed** (`.settings-ability-option-hint #767676 on selectedOption #f4f8ff is 4.26:1`);
- a hover override `#6a6a6a` on a correct base — "each surface passes" with two colours → **1 failed** (repainted hint).

`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` is clean. `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs` — 234 passed. The desktop unit suite reports 55 failing cases on this WSL host **both with and without the change** — the same files in both runs (the comparison is a `git stash` of this diff) — so they are pre-existing here, not this diff; the new test is green in both runs.

## Scope notes

- `.settings-ability-divider` ("或指定") is not in the report's table. It is the same colour and size, in the same block, on the same surface, and it read 2.43:1, so it moved with the rest; say the word if dividers should stay decorative instead.
- Rules with a hint colour that this report does not name are untouched — e.g. `.expert-desc` (`#8c8c8c`, 3.36:1 on white) in the 专家 flyout. They are the same defect on other rows and belong in a follow-up rather than silently widening this one.

## Merge order with #1491

**#1504 lands first.** This pull request is in the merge queue (`QUEUED`, enqueued 2026-11-27 11:05:29Z); #1491 has no merge-queue entry and is still `REVIEW_REQUIRED` (head `9b1881ae`).

Closes #1485.

The settings surface was modal for the pointer and not for the keyboard: opening it left `document.activeElement` on the 设置 button in the rail, the first Tab walked the page behind the backdrop, and Escape closed the panel without returning focus anywhere useful (#1485 measured 23 Tabs before the dialog was reached and 47 before the focus loop fell out to `BODY`).

**What changed** (four files: `SystemSettingsDialog.tsx`, `SettingsModal.tsx`, the new `settings-keyboard.spec.ts` and the map registration; +324/−3 across the pull request)

- the panel is now `<section role="dialog" tabIndex={-1} ref>` and an effect moves focus into it on open, remembering the element that opened it;
- a keydown trap keeps Tab inside the panel: at the last stop Tab wraps to the first, at the first Shift+Tab wraps to the last, and the panel itself counts as one end so the very first Tab enters the content instead of leaving;
- the focusable list is filtered with `getClientRects()` so hidden items are skipped, and it includes `summary`, which this panel really has (`McpServers.tsx:533`, `SandboxDirectSettings.tsx:147`, `SkillGitImportView.tsx:316`);
- Escape still closes through the existing window listener and `claimsEscape`; the trap's cleanup returns focus to the opener when that element is still connected (the skill-import and MCP-trial paths navigate away instead, so they are left alone);
- the panel keeps holding the boundary for the surfaces that trap nothing (添加模型 and the two skill dialogs), while a nested surface that does trap Tab claims the key first and the panel leaves it alone through `event.defaultPrevented` — that is `McpModal`, and also the skill drawer inside `SettingsModal` (`SettingsModal.tsx:58-72`), whose listener now sits on the drawer surface instead of on `document`. Without that move the panel handler, being closer to the target, ran first and swallowed the drawer's wrap: from 设置 › 专家 › 新增专家 › 指定可用能力 › 配置技能, Tab off the drawer's 确定 walked the form behind it instead of wrapping. The 新增专家 / 编辑专家 screens themselves are panel pages (`specialist-subpage`), not dialogs, so nothing there traps.

**Where focus lands, and why** — on the panel container, not on its first control. That is what `McpModal.tsx:89-109` and `SkillDialog.tsx:49` already do, and this surface should behave like those two rather than like a fourth variant. Two alternatives were built and photographed before choosing: the first focusable control here is the 收起侧栏 button (Enter collapses the navigation), and focusing the selected navigation item (`aria-current="page"`, 「通用」) would add a rule neither existing modal has. Switching to that second option later is a one-line change in the same effect, if it is wanted after seeing the frames.

**Evidence** — `apps/desktop/e2e/settings-keyboard.spec.ts`, six mocked desktop cases on real Tab presses:

1. opening the panel puts focus inside it, and the first Tab lands on a control inside it;
2. Shift+Tab from the panel goes to the last stop, Tab from the last wraps to the first, and 60 consecutive Tabs never leave the panel;

Mutation runs, each reverting one mechanism only: dropping `node.focus()` fails case 1; dropping the keydown listener fails case 2; dropping `previous.focus()` fails case 3; dropping the "panel holds focus" Shift+Tab branch fails case 2; putting the nested stand-aside back fails the 添加模型 case (that run was filtered to the single case, so it shows 1 failed and says nothing about the other four). The source was restored between runs and matched the committed bytes.

1512.body: ## Summary The desktop shell no longer opens an in-app web page for HUAWEI sign-in: it opens the account service in the **system default browser**, receives the one-shot ticket over a loopback callback, and forwards it to the renderer. - **Install-phase entry page** — after a successful sign-in the page shows the success panel (登录成功 / welcome / credits) with an 「进入工作台」 button. - **Account page (用户详情页)** — a settled sign-in swaps straight to the account details; the success summary belongs to the install phase only. - **Failure handling** — the install phase offers 「继续配置自定义模型」 or 「重试」; the account page keeps its signed-out state and offers 重试. - **No frozen page** — an in-flight sign-in can be cancelled while the browser leg is in flight (once the ticket is being exchanged there is nothing left to cancel) and times out after 5 minutes (Microsoft Entra allows 5 minutes per interactive step, Okta/Auth0 document 5-minute browser redirects, RFC 8628 device flows use 5–30 minutes). - Plain browsers (web build, SPA dev server, Playwright) keep the existing same-window fragment redirect. ## Changes | Area | File | What | |---|---|---| | Shell | `application/src/signin-callback.ts` | one-shot loopback callback server bound to a per-flow nonce (same-origin and JSON body only, single use, 16 KB body cap, 10-minute safety timeout) | | Shell | `application/src/main.ts`, `application/src/preload.ts` | `sd-shell:account-signin-*` IPC plus `shell.openExternal` for the built sign-in URL | | Renderer | `apps/desktop/src/auth/browser-signin.ts` | bridge wrapper, 5-minute deadline, cancel | | Renderer | `apps/desktop/src/views/LoginPage.tsx` | success panel, failure panel with the two ways forward, waiting hint and cancel | | Renderer | `apps/desktop/src/views/AccountPage.tsx` | system-browser sign-in from the account panel, details directly after success, retry after failure | | Copy | `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts` | new strings | | Tests | `application/test/signin-callback.test.ts`, `apps/desktop/tests/browser-signin.test.ts` | callback, cancel and timeout coverage | ## Validation Local run on Windows 10 22H2, Node 24.22.3, pnpm workspace: | Check | Result | |---|---| | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck` | pass | | `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build` | pass | | `node scripts/build.mjs` (shell bundle) | `shell build ok` | | `apps/desktop` targeted unit tests (browser-signin, shell-bridge, boot-screens, setup-wizard, account-gate, accounts-signin-notice) | 8 pass, 4 skipped (other platforms), 0 fail | | `apps/desktop` browser-signin unit tests (incl. cancel during `begin()`) | 6/6 pass | | `application` loopback callback tests (incl. wrong-flow, cross-site and foreign-origin posts) | 7/7 pass | | `apps/desktop` `onboarding-account.spec.ts` (desktop-chromium, after the rebase) | 7/7 pass | The screenshots below come from the built desktop UI served by the local stack, driven through a mocked shell bridge and a mocked account service so every state is deterministic and repeatable. Both languages were captured. ### 中文 | State | Screenshot | |---|---| | 01 安装配置页（入口） | | | 02 等待系统浏览器登录（5 分钟提示 + 取消登录） | | | 03 登录失败（继续配置自定义模型 / 重试） | | | 04 登录成功（欢迎 / 积分 / 进入工作台） | | | 05 用户详情页（未登录） | | | 06 用户详情页（登录成功后直接显示详情） | | ### English | State | Screenshot | |---|---| | 01 Install-phase entry page | | | 02 Waiting for the system browser (5-minute hint + cancel) | | | 03 Sign-in failed (custom model / try again) | | | 04 Signed in (welcome / credits / enter workspace) | | | 05 Account page (signed out) | | | 06 Account page (details shown right after sign-in) | | ### Notes - The screenshots are not committed to this branch: they live on the temporary `pr-1512-assets` branch, and the tables above pin them to commit `12a70738`, so the pixels this description shows cannot drift. They are review evidence, not part of the build. - The real end-to-end round-trip (system browser -> HUAWEI -> loopback callback -> desktop) was also exercised manually before these captures, with the shell's `SCIENCE_AGENT_ACCOUNTS_URL` set to `https://sciencediscovery.openjiuwen.com/accounts`. ### Review follow-up (commit `f7c68f66`) - **F1** — `test/source-test-map.json` maps `apps/desktop/src/auth/browser-signin.ts` to its unit test, so the changed-path gate can pass. - **F2** — the loopback callback is bound to a per-flow nonce (`/callback/` serves the page, `/result/` accepts the post; anything else is 404). A foreign `Origin`, a non-`same-origin` `Sec-Fetch-Site` and a non-`application/json` body are refused, and the page sends `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and a CSP. - **F3** — a flow cancelled while `begin()` is still in flight (or whose `open()` fails) now closes the just-created server instead of leaving it until its own timeout. - **F4** — the account panel awaits `onSignedIn` before leaving its pending state, and a rejection reaches the failure state. - **F5** — cancel is offered only while the browser leg is in flight, in both the install page and the account panel. - **F6** — the accounts deploy template moved out of this repository with #1492, so the `WEB_ORIGINS=http://127.0.0.1:*` line now belongs to the extracted accounts service's deployment template; the rebase dropped this branch's edit of that file. - **F7** — the system-browser page is bilingual; that browser's language is not readable from the app. - The screenshots are no longer committed to this branch; they moved to the temporary `pr-1512-assets` branch, pinned to commit `12a70738`, and the 02 frames were refreshed for the narrower, left-aligned cancel action. Rebased onto `main` (`4f3d75ed`, which includes #1492's merge `90e736bc`): `settleAuthTicket` now calls #1492's `exchangeTicket(ticket)` signature, and the deleted accounts deploy template is no longer edited here.

Of the 95 files, 79 are `.png`, 6 are `.jpg` and 10 are the `README.md` files that describe the older sets. This includes `1440`, added on 2026-11-27 (18:04:07Z) — the most recent committed set.

## Why

#1477 records the convention that UI frames are review evidence, not repository artifacts: they are hosted outside the tree at a URL that does not change, embedded in the pull request body, and pinned to a commit SHA when that URL comes from a branch. Those directories are history rather than the rule, and the tree still carries that history. Git keeps every one of them: each blob stays reachable from the commit that added it, so this change removes them from the current tree without losing them.

## What this does not break, checked rather than assumed

- **In-tree references: exactly one.** `apps/desktop/e2e/network-allowlist.spec.ts:48` is the only file on `main` that names a path under `docs/screenshots/`, in the comment "The screenshots each run writes are copied unchanged into `docs/screenshots/1399/`…". I downloaded and grepped the contents of all 1,034 text files on `main` (`.md`, `.mjs`, `.json`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.sh`, `.py`, `.txt`, `.html`, `.spec.ts`, and `.ts`/`.tsx` under `scripts/` or `e2e/`). Several files discuss screenshots in general — `.ci/README.md`, `.agents/skills/frontend-quality/{SKILL.md,references/*}`, `docs/en/design/desktop-mcp-controls.v2.md`, `docs/en/developer-docs/frontend-quality.md` among them — and every one of those mentions the word, not this path: no link, no path, nothing that resolves into the directory. There is also no index `README.md` at `docs/screenshots/`.
- **The one comment is comment-only and does not read this directory.** It says a run copies its captures there for review evidence; no test reads or writes those files, so the capture behaviour is unchanged by deleting them. #1477 already rewrites that same comment (`:47-49`) to say the frames are attached to the pull request.
- **Pull request bodies: none point into `main`.** Of the 116 pull requests that mention `docs/screenshots`, I read every body: no body links or embeds a path on `main`/`master`. Recent ones embed frames from a fork branch or from an upstream commit SHA (for example `…/3df4eb11…/docs/screenshots/1503/…`), and those keep resolving because the commits still exist.

## The guide's wording is a follow-up, not part of this change

#1477 adds a `### UI changes need screenshots` section to `CONTRIBUTING.md` whose two sentences describe these directories as still present:

> Some directories under `docs/screenshots/` still hold frames committed by earlier changes; that is history, not the rule…

> Some of the committed directories kept that in a `README.md`; the rest left it in the pull request that added them…

After this change both clauses describe directories that no longer exist. Those lines are **not on `main` yet** — #1477 introduces them — so editing them here would race that pull request on the same file for no benefit. So this PR deliberately does not touch `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and the wording correction follows in a separate change once #1477 has landed: both sentences move to the past tense (planned: "…held frames committed by earlier changes…" and "The directories that held committed frames kept that in a `README.md`…"). Until then the guide is no more wrong than it is today, and after this change it is wrong only about the tense.

## Verification for this head

- Merge base is `main` = `e374837d`; the branch is one commit that changes no file except the 95 deletions.
- The tree I built was diffed against `main` before pushing: `docs/screenshots/` has no remaining entry, and no other path changed (the `docs` tree node's own sha moves, which is the consequence of its child changing).
- No test suite applies to deleting documentation image files; the reference audit above is the evidence, and its inputs are named so it can be repeated.

1521.author: yuanzhou75
1521.body:
Closes #1520

Two independent assumptions in the import path made a freshly exported package fail to import. #1520 reproduced both against real packages; this fixes each where it breaks and pins it with a test that fails when the fix is reverted.

## Root cause 1 — a version object the package does not carry killed the restore (`404 File not found`)

`records.versionObjects` names every version the session's records point at, including the ones the exporter could not read. One real package carries **271** `version:…:unavailable source object` lines in `manifest.omissions`, the same **271** refs still in `records.versionObjects`, and **none** of their objects in `archive/objects` — the package is honest, and the import died on the first one.

The two import paths disagreed about their own interface:

- `importResearchPackage` builds a `Map`, so a missing object is `undefined` and the existing `if (object)` guards skip it;
- `importResearchPackageStreamed` builds `DirectoryObjects` (`packages/research-package/src/index.ts`), which is declared as a `PackageObjectDirectory extends ReadonlyMap<string, Uint8Array>` but whose `get` was `readFileSync` — a miss threw `ENOENT`, and the server turned that into `404 {"error":"File not found"}`.

**Fix.** `DirectoryObjects.get` answers a miss with `undefined`, exactly like the map it claims to be; the read that iterates its own listing keeps using a private `read`. Every existing guard in `restorePackage` then works for both import paths, and nothing else changes.

The version restore no longer stays silent when a package does *not* declare the loss: it records `version:<pool>:<digest>:missing object`, but only when the package has not already said so — so the 271 declared ones are still reported once, not twice.

## Root cause 2 — a tool record's citation list was rewritten as a composer reference (`400 Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')`)

`remapRunEvent` decided by **key name only**: anything reached under a key called `references` was cast to `ComposerReference` and had its `id` rewritten. A tool call keeps its own citation list under that same name —

```json
{ "refsource": "Water Res. 2015 Nov 1;84():378", "reftype": "Erratum in", "pmid": "", "note": "" }
```

— with no `kind` and no `id`. The rewrite called `ids.id(undefined)`, `source.match` threw, and a valid import answered `400` with that raw JavaScript message, which the dialog shows verbatim. One package carried eight of them.

**Fix.** A reference is rewritten only when it actually carries a string `id`; anything else is walked and left exactly as it is. The composer's own references still get the new namespace, so this is a shape test rather than switching the rewrite off.

## Evidence

`packages/research-package/src/stream-import.test.ts` — a streamed package's object map answers `undefined` for a path it does not carry, the same as the in-memory map (previously threw `ENOENT`).

`services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts` — two HTTP cases over the real `inspect`/`import` route with the streamed path:

1. a package whose `records.versionObjects` names an object the archive does not carry imports with `201` and reports `version:agent-state:<digest>:missing object`;
2. a version the package already declared unreadable is reported **once**, not twice.

`services/api/src/research-package-history.test.ts` (new) — a run event whose only `references` entry is such a citation comes back deep-equal, while a composer reference is still remapped.

**Mutation runs**, each reverting one mechanism:

| mutation | result |
| --- | --- |
| `DirectoryObjects.get` throws again | `stream-import.test.ts` 9/10 (the new parity case red) |
| the same, with `packages/research-package` rebuilt so the API sees it | `research-package-http.test.ts` 29/31 (both new cases red) |
| the shape guard removed | `research-package-history.test.ts` 0/1 |
| the `missing object` line removed (back to silent skip) | `research-package-http.test.ts` 30/31 — the "says so" case red; the once-only case still passes there, because the package's own declared line is what it counts |

**Suites run**, on the exact bytes pushed: `research-package/src/{index,stream-import,json}.test.ts` 18 + 10 + 3, `research-package-http` 31, `research-package-history` 1, `research-package-preflight` 11, `research-package-necessary` 4, `research-snapshot-integrity` 21, `shell-executions` 62 — **161 passed, 0 failed**. `tsc -p services/api`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` and `tsc -p packages/research-package` all exit 0.

## Not verified here

- The four `.sdresearch` files from the report are on the reporter's machine; both failing shapes are pinned with packages built in the tests rather than with those exact files.
- The full UT/ST layers, L1/L2, `merge-gate` and a real backend were not run locally; CI is their evidence.
- No user-visible surface changes: the import dialog already renders the receipt's omission list, and this only changes what reaches it (`201` plus an omission instead of `404`/`400`).

1530.body:
Closes #1515

## What changes

`GET /api/search` matched Project names, Session titles (plus project name and Session id) and artifact names/titles — never a message body — so a phrase that exists only inside a conversation found nothing. `searchWorkbench` now also matches message bodies for a non-empty query, and returns the conversation as the **same** `kind: "session"` hit it already returns, carrying:

- `snippet` — the latest line of the transcript that contains the query, clipped around the match with `…` on the cut side, at most 200 characters. Cuts land on code points, so a clipped line never ends in half an emoji. New optional field on `WorkbenchSearchResult`; `detail` stays the Project line it was.

No new result kind, so `limit`/`offset`/`hasMore`/`total`, ordering and the project/session/artifact filters keep their meaning, and both clients keep their existing result list.

## The scan is bounded, not exhaustive

A transcript is one JSON file read whole (`services/api/src/store.ts:7319`), and nothing indexes it, so this is deliberately a bounded scan rather than "search everything":

| bound | value |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions read per query | the 200 most recently updated live Sessions outside the inbox |
| Messages scanned per Session | the newest 500, counting back from the last turn |
| Message-body characters scanned per Session | the newest 2,000,000, spent from the last turn backwards |
| Serialized transcript bytes charged per query | 8,000,000 |

Both per-Session bounds are spent from the newest turn backwards: a transcript is stored oldest-first, so a long Session loses its oldest text to the budget rather than its newest, and the matching line reported for a Session is its latest one. Each Session is charged the size of the transcript `readMessages` actually parsed (including `modelContext` and keys outside the body), not the text up to the first hit, so a hit cannot under-count the budget. A title hit is never re-read and never appears twice; an exact Session id is a lookup that reads no transcript; archived and inbox Sessions are never content-searched.

**Residual, stated rather than hidden:** one unusually large transcript is still read whole before it is charged, so a query can cost one full parse of such a file. That is the price of having no index; a real index is a separate change.

## Both clients

- Desktop search dialog: the matching line is a third row under the Project line (`search-hit-snippet`), so a long Project name cannot ellipsize the reason the row is there. `searchSnippet` refuses a snippet on a non-session hit.
- Web composer palette: it draws the same row and keeps a content hit when its client-side filter matches only the snippet.
- `zh-CN` and `en` hint and empty state no longer claim that message text is not searched.

## Relation to the closed #1519

#1519 was closed by the maintainer's decision that this account lands the change, on the same shape. This branch starts from that implementation: I re-read it against the route, the store read path, the shared schema and both clients, ran every gate below myself, and fixed the one thing its review flagged as non-blocking — the `MockOptions.search` doc comment in `apps/desktop/e2e/fixtures.ts` still said the mock matches `label` only, while it also matches `snippet`. No behavioural divergence.

## What I ran

## Summary

When `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is on, `merge_group` runs already send `UT` and the three heavy mocked shards to the self-hosted pool `[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`. This PR routes the remaining credential-free Linux L2 jobs there too:

- `ST`
- `L2 E2E (mocked, governed)` and `L2 E2E (mocked, literature)`
- `Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E`

Pull requests, every other event, hosted runs, credentialed real E2E jobs and distribution jobs are unchanged.

## Why

Merge-queue runs between 05:15 and 07:22 UTC on 2026-11-28 (423 jobs):

| Pool | Average utilisation | Peak concurrency | Queue time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Self-hosted heavy | 28% of 36 runners | 28 | ≈0 (max 0.1 min) |
| Hosted, for the jobs moved here | — | — | median 3.9–6.0 min, max 15.6–20.2 min |

| Job (hosted) | Run (median) | Queue (median / max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop UI-ST and mocked E2E | 8.7 min | 3.9 / 18.1 min |
| ST | 4.7 min | 5.1 / 15.6 min |
| L2 mocked governed | 3.5 min | 5.4 / 20.2 min |
| L2 mocked literature | 3.2 min | 6.0 / 18.0 min |

The slowest self-hosted L2 job (`standard-config`) takes about 12.7 min. The L2 stage as a whole had a median of 17.7 min and a maximum of 26.3 min. In 5 of the 11 fully green runs, the job that finished L2 last was one of these hosted jobs. The self-hosted pool has since grown to 52 heavy runners across three hosts, so moving these four jobs should bring L2 close to the `standard-config` bound.

## Changes

- `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`: `HEAVY_MOCKED_SHARDS` becomes `SELF_HOSTED_MOCKED_SHARDS` and lists all five mocked shards. A newly added shard stays hosted until someone lists it.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  - `st` and `desktop-mocked` use `runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.policy.outputs.ut_runner) }}`, the same policy output and pool as UT.
  - Both drop the remote `cache: pnpm` on the self-hosted path; `st` also drops the uv cache.
  - `st` provisions bubblewrap with `sudo` only when `bwrap` does not already work, using the same check as UT and the mocked E2E job.
  - On self-hosted, `st` skips `actions/cache` for the verified CPython archive and points `BINARY_CACHE_DIR` at the persistent `/ci-cache/binary-cache`. `fetch-runtime.mjs` already creates that directory and stages each write before renaming it into place.
  - On self-hosted, `desktop-mocked` runs `playwright install chromium` without `--with-deps`. The runner image already carries Chromium's system libraries and grants no `sudo`.
- `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: the contract now expects all five shards to be routed, and checks the new routing, cache and no-sudo wiring for `st` and `desktop-mocked`. `docker` and the binary jobs must stay hosted.
- `.ci/README.md`: the self-hosted routing section lists the new jobs and what stays hosted.

## Validation

- `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`: 246 tests, 246 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm ci:l1`: PASS, planned 4, executed 4, passed 4.
- `pnpm ci:selftest`: passed.
- `pnpm docs:check`: passed (148 Markdown files).
- The four moved jobs, reproduced at `main` `a19476ae2` inside temporary containers. Each container used the self-hosted runner image and the same container options as the registered runners, was not registered with GitHub, and ran the steps as this workflow now runs them on self-hosted (no `sudo`, no remote caches, local `/ci-cache`):

  | Job | Result | Wall time incl. clone and install |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | ST (`pnpm ci:st -- --profile merge --coverage`) | PASS 69/69 | 4.2 min |
  | mocked `governed` (`pnpm ci:e2e -- --profile merge --shard governed`) | PASS 5/5 | 2.1 min |
  | mocked `literature` (`--shard literature`) | PASS 6/6 | 2.0 min |
  | Desktop: `run-desktop-e2e.mjs ui-st` and `mocked` with `CI_DESKTOP_SPECS=all`, `CI_DESKTOP_PROFILE=merge` | 14 passed + 254 passed, 0 failed | 4.9 min |

- UT and the other mocked shards were not re-run on this commit: the change only touches CI orchestration, and those jobs keep their existing routing.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable as a product change. No user-observable behaviour changes. The journeys these jobs run were executed unchanged on the self-hosted image as listed above.

## Risk and rollout

- This changes the CI contract (workflow routing), so it needs maintainer confirmation.
- Self-hosted runners only receive trusted `merge_group` runs. The policy fails closed to `ubuntu-latest` for `pull_request`, forks and every other event.
- Rollback: unset or change `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE`. Newly created merge-queue runs then go back to `ubuntu-latest`; runs that were already queued for self-hosted labels need to be cancelled and re-queued.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

User impact: none; merge-queue validation runs on different runners.

Compatibility and migration: no migration. The self-hosted runners already provide `/ci-cache`, bubblewrap and Chromium's system libraries.

1537.author: HongyeZhou
1537.body:
## Problem

Nightly L4 run 44361037291 (head `d57fc269`) failed on `research-2` / DRB-59 with `[181001] model call failed ... read ECONNRESET` and delivered partial. `stack.log` shows the request `model-8f784f89` was HTTP 200 with 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes / 105,894 ms, `hasText` and `hasToolCalls` true, `finishReason: "tool_calls"` — and then `error.classification: "network"`, `attempts: 1`, `retries: 0`. The provider had declared the turn complete; the gateway reset the connection before `[DONE]`, and the turn was discarded.

## Root cause

All three protocols read through the shared `sseData` reader (`packages/model/src/client.ts`), but only the chat reader wraps it with `canRecoverAfterCompletion`. The Responses and Anthropic readers iterate `sseData` without that guard, so a transport failure after their terminal record (`response.completed` / `message_delta`) propagates and the parsed turn is lost.

On this base the chat reader already carries the guard, so DRB-59's exact protocol no longer reproduces there — the same defect is still live for the other two protocols that share the reader, and there was no transport-level test at all (only gateway-level tests that inject a fake streamer).

## Change

- Adds `sseDataWithRecovery`, a thin wrapper around `sseData` that takes the caller's live completion state and ends the iteration normally when the transport fails after a terminal record was seen; a failure before that still propagates.
- The Responses reader passes `response.completed` / `response.incomplete` as its terminal state, the Anthropic reader maps `stop_reason` to the canonical finish reasons (`tool_use` → `tool_calls`, `max_tokens` → `length`, otherwise `stop`).
- Both readers keep the chat path's post-recovery guard: a recovered turn with incomplete tool arguments still throws.
- `jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts` is untouched, as are `MAX_STREAM_RETRIES` and the "do not replay once text was sent" policy — that policy is by design and out of scope here.

## Red / green evidence

New file `packages/model/src/client-transport.test.ts` drives a real HTTP server, writes the frames, and destroys the socket without `[DONE]`.

Before (`client.ts` at `4f3d75ed`, new tests only):

```
ok 1 - a chat stream reset after finish_reason still returns the completed turn
not ok 2 - a Responses stream reset after response.completed still returns the completed turn
not ok 3 - an Anthropic stream reset after message_delta still returns the completed turn
not ok 4 - a recovered Responses turn with truncated tool arguments is still rejected
ok 5 - a stream reset before finish_reason still fails
# tests 5
# pass 2
# fail 3
```

After (this PR):

```
ok 1 - a chat stream reset after finish_reason still returns the completed turn
ok 2 - a Responses stream reset after response.completed still returns the completed turn
ok 3 - an Anthropic stream reset after message_delta still returns the completed turn
ok 4 - a recovered Responses turn with truncated tool arguments is still rejected
ok 5 - a stream reset before finish_reason still fails
# tests 5
# pass 5
# fail 0
```

Case 1 is a regression guard for the protocol DRB-59 used; cases 2 and 3 are the defect this PR fixes; case 4 covers the post-recovery tool-argument guard on the new path; case 5 pins that a stream reset before any terminal record is still an error.

## Test collection

The tagged node audit requires each `test(...)` callback to be a static arrow or function expression, so every case is registered as `test("…", async () => { await runAfterCompletionCase(...); })`. `node --import tsx test/support/tagged/node-collect.mjs` with this file collects 5 identities, and `node test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile pr --slice ut` now gets past the node phase. That slice then stops at its *python* collection phase in this worktree (no `uv` environment built here), so the UT job on CI is the real confirmation of the whole slice.

## Verification

- `node --import tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts"` in `packages/model` — 173 tests, 173 pass, 0 fail
- `tsc -p packages/model` — clean
- `pnpm ci:l1` — PASS, planned 4 / passed 4 / failed 0
- Real L4/L5 E2E was not run locally: it needs `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL`, `E2E_LLM_MODEL`, `E2E_LLM_TOKEN` and quota, which this environment does not have; the nightly run is the real-layer check.

## Reproduction

1. Start an HTTP SSE endpoint that writes a chat/Responses/Anthropic stream with its terminal record and then destroys the socket without `[DONE]`.
2. Call `streamModelTurn` against it.
3. Before this PR the Responses and Anthropic calls reject with a network-classified error; with this PR they return the parsed turn, while the same reset before the terminal record still rejects.

## Files

- `packages/model/src/client.ts` — `sseDataWithRecovery`, the two reader call sites, the post-recovery tool-argument guard.
- `packages/model/src/client-transport.test.ts` — new transport-level cases.

Fixes #1238

Closes #1540

## What changes

A corrupt, truncated or simply wrong file uploaded to `POST /api/projects/<id>/research-package/inspect` or `.../import` answered `500 {"error":"Internal server error"}`: the decompressor's `Z_DATA_ERROR` / `Z_BUF_ERROR` and the archive parser's own refusal sentences were never classified, so the log line was `unclassified_request_error` and the dialog showed an internal error for the caller's own file.

`services/api/src/http/research-package-refusal.ts` maps them, and the global handler asks it before the generic branch:

| input | answer |
| --- | --- |
| random bytes / a file that is not gzip (`Z_DATA_ERROR`, `incorrect header check`, `not in gzip format`) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID` |
| a truncated archive (`Z_BUF_ERROR`, `unexpected end of file`) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TRUNCATED` |
| a package the parser refused (bad manifest, checksum mismatch, unlisted entry, unsafe path, ...) | `400` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_INVALID`, with the parser's sentence in parentheses |
| a metadata entry over its bound | `413` `RESEARCH_PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE` |

Each answer carries an `error` sentence the import dialog can show — "This file is not a valid research package: it ends before the archive does." — instead of an internal-error string, so the two endpoints now behave like the refusals that already work (`507` capacity, `409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`).

**The exception list is deliberate.** The refusal sentences are named one by one rather than "any error from the parser is the caller's fault": exporter-side faults (`A synchronous export cannot stream package objects`, `Package object size changed while hashing`), filesystem failures (`ENOSPC`, `EACCES`, ...) and every failure outside the two upload paths keep their `500`. The direction of the trade is written in the module: a refusal the parser adds later keeps its `500` until it is classified here, which is the safe way to be wrong.

## What I ran

- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-invalid.test.ts` (new, api) — **4/4 pass**. The endpoint test posts the four payloads #1540 measured — 64 KiB of random bytes, an archive truncated to half, a 12-byte gzip header, `{"hello":"world"}` — to **both** endpoints (8 requests) and asserts `400`, a stable `code`, an `error` sentence containing "not a valid research package", and that the body is not `Internal server error`.
- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-http.test.ts` (existing, api) — **29/29 pass**, so the `413` / `507` / `409` answers that already existed are unaffected.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck` — clean.
- Mutation: deleting the new branch from the global handler turns the endpoint test red with exactly the reported symptom — `inspect: 64 KiB of random bytes answered 500 {"error":"Internal server error"}` — and restoring it brings the suite back to 4/4.
- Classifier unit tests pin both directions: the parser's refusals map to 4xx, and an exporter fault, `ENOSPC` and a non-upload path stay `undefined` (500).

## Scope

Backend only: no client change and no visual change, so no screenshots. The dialog already renders `error` from a 4xx package refusal.

Files: `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (the branch, 7 lines), `services/api/src/http/research-package-refusal.ts` (new), `services/api/src/research-package-invalid.test.ts` (new). None of them is in #1521, whose change is in `packages/research-package/src/index.ts` and `services/api/src/research-snapshots.ts`, so the two PRs do not collide.

## Changes

A plain `Error` is still decided by the legacy prose list, so a hand-written internal `throw new Error("… must …")` outside a validator still answers `400` — that residual is deliberate (the list is what keeps the established validator 400s) and disappearing it would need every such thrower migrated to `ApiStatusError` or a stable code.

API-level: the new tests drive the running server over a socket; no browser surface changed.

Release category: release:fix
User impact: internal faults no longer surface as 400s carrying JavaScript text.
Compatibility and migration: none.

1551.author: yuanzhou75
1551.body:
Closes #1533.

The request catch-all decides whether a failure was the caller's mistake by matching words in the error message, and answers `400` with that message as the body (`services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `isKnownClientInputError(error)` → `sendError(response, 400, message)`). An internal fault whose text happens to say "cannot", "invalid" or "must" therefore reaches the client as a client error, carrying JavaScript that was never written for a reader. #1520's import did exactly that:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match')
```

matched /cannot/, so the dialog showed that sentence and the status said the caller was wrong while the server was.

## What changed — three gates in the classifier, one boundary for JSON bodies

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.ts` decides three things before it reads the wording list:

- `isRuntimeFault`: `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `ReferenceError` and `EvalError` are the interpreter reporting a defect in this server, so their message is not evidence about the caller. The three shapes #1533 names (`Cannot read properties of undefined`, `Invalid array length`, `Cannot convert undefined or null to object`) are pinned by a test.
- `quotesInterpreterFault`: the engine's own sentences, matched on the text, so a handler that re-wraps `cause.message` in a plain `Error` cannot put them back: `Cannot read|set properties of undefined|null`, `Cannot convert …`, `Cannot create property … on string|number|symbol`, `Cannot destructure …`, `Cannot use 'in' operator …`, `is not a function|iterable|defined`, `Invalid array length|string length`, `Maximum call stack size exceeded`, `Assignment to constant variable`. One representative sentence per pattern is pinned; the patterns keep the part that makes the wording unmistakable, so a validator sentence (`after_ms must be a positive integer`) does not match.
- `carriesExplicitCode`: a non-empty string `code` is a label from the layer that raised the error — Node's `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`, the filesystem's `ENOTDIR`, or a handler that already knows the answer. #1533 names an explicit code as a legitimate source of a `400` beside `ApiStatusError`, so the code, not the prose, decides: the catch-all answers the codes it knows (`CONFLICT`, `INVALID_UPLOAD_PATH`, `SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_INVALID`, …) before this classifier runs.
- `SyntaxError` stays a client error: a body that does not parse is the caller's own bytes.
- A plain `Error` whose text is ordinary prose keeps the existing wording rules, because that list is a record of what the legacy validators say — deleting it would turn every one of their `400`s into a `500`, which is the opposite failure.

Narrowing the classifier exposes every place that turned a caller's malformed body into an interpreter fault, so that is fixed where the input enters:

- `services/api/src/http/body.ts`: `readJson` refuses a JSON body that is not an object (`null`, an array, a string, a number) with `ApiStatusError(400, "Request body must be a JSON object")`. It sits on top of `readJsonValue`, which is the old parse-only behaviour and is kept for routes that define their own body-shape contract: the two environment install/uninstall routes validate `packages` themselves and must answer `packages must be an array of strings` for `{}`, a `null` body or a non-list. Every other object body goes through `readJson`, so the refusal covers 82 call sites today and any added later, instead of a per-route guard the next route can forget.
- `services/api/src/http/index.ts`: `readSpecialistBody` existed only to apply the object check on two routes; it is deleted and both call sites use `readJson`, which now owns the rule. Nothing else in the catch-all changes — the `SKILL_VALIDATION` code-to-status line this change needed earlier is already on `main`, so after the rebase it is not part of the diff.

`readOptionalJson` is deliberately unchanged: `undefined` means "no body", and its two callers already pass the parsed value through `extractReplacementModelId`, which answers `ApiStatusError(400, "Deletion options must be an object")` for a non-object.

## Honest boundary

The guarantee this change makes is: **no interpreter-raised fault, no error carrying an interpreter sentence, and no error carrying an explicit code is answered `400` or echoed.** Those get `500`, `{"error":"Internal server error"}`, and an `unclassified_request_error` line holding the original text.

Three residues remain, all deliberate:

- An `Error` thrown by our own code whose message is ordinary prose containing "cannot", "must" or "invalid", with no code and no interpreter shape — `cannot open the catalog database`, say — is still answered `400` with its text. The prose list cannot tell an internal sentence from a validator's; closing that residue means giving the legacy validators typed errors (`ApiStatusError`) across the stores.
- A coded *client* rejection whose code is missing from the catch-all's table answers `500` instead of falling back to its prose. That is the direction #1533 asks for ("a `400` comes from something that knows the input was wrong"); the code table is what keeps that list complete, and the one code in that position at this branch point (`SKILL_VALIDATION`) is mapped on `main`.
- An object endpoint that receives a JSON body which parses but is not an object now answers `400 Request body must be a JSON object` instead of being destructured, spread or ignored. The environment install/uninstall routes keep their own wording for that case, because their contract names the field.

## Evidence

`services/api/src/http/error-classification.test.ts` — five cases: the wording list's established 400s; the length-rejection boundary; runtime faults of every class; sixteen engine sentences on a plain `Error` (one of them prefixed with a handler's own sentence); and coded errors (`ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`, `ENOTDIR`, `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`) as not-client-input, with an empty `code` still decided by its sentence.

`services/api/src/http/internal-error-http.test.ts` — four route cases. Three throw a fault once from inside the request handler — a `TypeError`, a plain `Error` carrying the engine's sentence, and a coded `cannot start a transaction within a transaction` — and each must answer `500` with `{"error":"Internal server error"}`, free of the fault's text, plus an `unclassified_request_error` line asserted against the real `apiLog`. The fourth keeps a legacy validator rejection (`Specialist name is required`) at `400` with its own wording, so a future change cannot quiet the whole path instead of narrowing it.

`services/api/src/web-settings-api.test.ts` — the four non-object bodies answer `400` with `Request body must be a JSON object`, which is the case that was red in `UT` on an earlier head of this change.

`services/api/src/specialists-http.test.ts` — still 17 cases green, including "a body that parses to a non-object is a 400, not a server fault", which now passes through `readJson`'s rule.

**Mutations**, each restored to bytes matching the commit:

- remove `if (quotesInterpreterFault(error.message)) return false;` → its unit case fails (`expected false, actual true`) and the plain-`Error` route case fails;
- remove `if (carriesExplicitCode(error)) return false;` → the coded unit case and the coded route case fail;
- remove the `readJson` object refusal → `web-settings-api.test.ts` fails again (the reported failure).

**No validator's `400` turns into a `500` by wording:** every string literal in `services/api/src` and `packages/*/src` (461 files, 59,290 literals without expressions, test files excluded) was classified by the base classifier and by this one; the number whose answer changed is **0**. The scan covers message text only — the code rule is not visible to it and is covered by the suites instead.

**Base comparison** on this machine: `web-settings-api.test.ts` is green at the branch point `a117ae99`, red on an earlier head of this change, green here; the skill lifecycle case is green at `a117ae99`, red on that head, green here. The two `model.usage` event-list failures in `server.test.ts` fail at `a117ae99` as well, so they are not this change's.

## Checks on this head (`9ae407cf`)

Local runs on the pre-rebase tree (`a117ae99`), where the five changed files are byte-identical to this head's:

- `pnpm exec tsc -p services/api --noEmit` → exit 0
- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` → exit 0
- `error-classification.test.ts` → 5 passed; `internal-error-http.test.ts` → 4 passed; `web-settings-api.test.ts` → 6 passed; neighbour `specialists-http.test.ts` → 17 passed
- full `services/api` suite → 2446 tests, 2437 pass, 7 fail: 5 need the Python sidecars this worktree does not have (`spawn …/services/evolve/.venv/bin/python ENOENT`, `…/services/paper/.venv/bin/python ENOENT`), 2 are the pre-existing `model.usage` event-list failures above

The first `UT` run on the rebased head found one real break: `server.test.ts::environment mutations preserve Runner not-found errors, isolate Runner auth failures and reject malformed package lists` sends a `null` body to `/api/environments/:id/install` and requires `400 packages must be an array of strings`, which the entry gate had turned into `400 Request body must be a JSON object`. `readJsonValue` is the fix described above; the environment routes are the only call sites that use it.

Not verified here: the full `UT`/`ST` layers, `L1`/`L2`, `merge-gate` and a real backend — CI is their evidence. The repository's tests declare `os:linux`; the runs above were on this host with the declarations honoured.

No user-visible surface changes: this is the status code and body of a failure path, and no stylesheet or component is touched.

1553.author: zhaozhaozz
1553.body:
Several UT cases waited for background work by polling a fixed number of times with a short sleep, so their real budget was `attempts × interval` plus whatever each poll cost: 0.5 s to 5 s. On a self-hosted merge-queue host shared with other heavy jobs the same work runs 1.2–3.5× slower, finishes correctly, and the case still fails on a state assertion (#1546 lists the cases and jobs). This moves every case named in the issue and its follow-up comment to a wall-clock deadline that reports the last observed state, and takes the RACE case's downloads out of its time budget. No product code changes.

## A deadline-based wait helper

`test/helpers/wait-until.ts` adds `waitUntil(observe, done, options)`. It observes, returns the first observation `done` accepts, and otherwise pauses and observes again until a wall-clock deadline (60 s by default), always repeating the observation once the deadline has passed so the failure reports a current state: `<description> was not reached within 60000 ms (N checks in M ms); last observed: <state>`. A passing case returns as soon as the state is reached, so it is not slower. An error thrown by `observe` fails the wait at once instead of being retried. `pause` is replaceable so the React fixture can let `act()` flush between observations. `test/helpers/wait-until.unit.ts` covers the immediate return, the repeated observation, the deadline message, a slow observation, a throwing observation and message truncation.

## The waits moved to it

- `services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts`: `waitForRunStatus` (was 200 × 25 ms) and `waitForGatewayTurn` (was 400 or 2400 × 25 ms) use the 60 s deadline; the delegated case keeps its swarm-sized budget as 90 s. The timeout names the run, the expected status, the last status and whether the replay had recorded it.
- `services/api/src/research-package-http.test.ts`: the six continuation polls (100 × 50 ms each, including the two at the lines the issue names) go through one `settledContinuation` helper that starts from the answer that created the operation, so the request sequence is unchanged.
- `services/runner/src/server.test.ts`: the managed-execution poll (100 × 5 ms) and the five NPU job polls (300 × 10 ms) wait until the state leaves `queued`/`running`; a job that fails now reaches its assertion at once instead of after the whole budget.
- `test/fixtures/app-progress-integration.test.mjs`: `mountRecordedApp` no longer loops 50 × 10 ms and falls through. The two cases that need the stored run's timeline wait for it with `renderedToolTimeline`, which fails naming what was rendered. The replacement-token case used to rely on those 0.5 s implicitly; it now waits for the cold-start request it depends on and for the rejection notice.
- `services/api/src/server.test.ts`: `startTestApi` returns once `/health` stops answering 503 `liveness: "starting"`. Every other route already waits for startup; only cases asserting on `/health` saw it, and `API health is degraded when the Runner answers without its detail` had the same race as the case the issue names. A failed startup (`unavailable`) still returns, so the case that caused it reports it. The timeout-settings case's two 10 s loops (detached Shell completion and the completion-notification drain) and the fixture teardown drain use the helper.
- `jiuwen_swarm/tests/test_mcp_boundary.py`: the 100 concurrent calls share one 60 s deadline instead of 3 s each. The deadline is passed to `call_tool(..., timeout=…)` as well; the pinned JiuwenSwarm timeout patch prefers that over the client's configured 5 s, so the SDK limit does not take over. The fixture's uvicorn start wait (200 × 10 ms) becomes a deadline too. Every other case keeps its budgets.

## RACE downloads move into preparation

`scripts/race-contract.test.mjs` ran `.ci/run-research-python.sh race` under a 120 s `execFileSync` timeout, and on a cold cache that run cloned `deep_research_bench` and resolved Python 3.14 and the pinned wheels first. The script gains a `prepare` mode that does exactly those downloads, and the shared runner runs it with the other UT preparation steps (`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`). The case itself is unchanged. On an empty cache `prepare` fetched about 570 MB (evaluator checkout 201 MB, interpreter 110 MB, wheels and metadata 261 MB) in 37 s here; afterwards `race` ran its 21 tests with `UV_OFFLINE=1` in 3.6 s, so nothing inside the case touches the network. It also stops `check:research-python-ut` and the RACE case from cloning into the same directory concurrently on a cold job.

## Validation

Host: 14 cores. "Busy loops" are `node -e 'for(;;){}'` processes, the stand-in for `stress-ng --cpu "$(nproc)"` (not installed here).

**Layers on the pushed head `1fefa189f`** (rebased on `dd5cc323a`):

- UT, `pnpm ci:ut -- --profile merge --coverage` with 14 busy loops running beside it: PASS in 24 min, planned 8937 / executed 8937 / passed 8937 / failed 0 / skipped 0 / blocked 0, 0 retried cases. Every case named in the issue and its comment ran and passed in it, as did the 6 new `wait-until.unit.ts` cases. The RACE case and `check:research-python-ut` (37 + 21 tests) logged no clone and no download: the new preparation step had fetched everything first.
- L1, `pnpm ci:l1`: PASS, 4/4.
- ST: `check:swarm-sdk-contract` (`.ci/run-research-python.sh contract`) twice beside 14 busy loops: 80 passed each time. The rest of the ST layer was not run; no other ST source changed.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` clean; the helper and its unit test type-check on their own as well.

**Before and after under load**: the issue's version `40a50e010` against this change, one file at a time, same load. These ran on the same patch before the rebase (identical `git patch-id`).

| Case | Load | `40a50e010` | This change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run-cancel.test.ts` on JiuwenSwarm (13 cases) | 42 busy loops, 4 runs | 4/4 runs red: 7 failures of `expected run … to become completed`, actual `'running'`, in `GET session usage reports…` and `a multi-turn run's usage row…`. After each red run the process never exited (servers left open) and had to be killed | 4/4 runs 13/13; those two cases took 7.7–19.3 s |
| `test_mcp_boundary.py` (24 cases) | 42 busy loops, 5 runs | 5/5 runs red: `test_100_concurrent_calls_keep_identity_and_execute_once`, `TimeoutError` | 5/5 runs 24/24 |
| runner `server.test.ts`, managed recovery + NPU Broker (9 cases) | 14 busy loops, test at `nice 10`, 3 runs | 1/3 runs red: `managed recovery HTTP contract…`, `'running' !== 'completed'` | 3/3 runs 9/9; also 2/2 at `nice 19` |
| API `server.test.ts`, the two `API health …` cases | 14 busy loops, test at `nice 19`, 2 runs | 2/2 runs red: both cases `503 !== 200` | no 503; `API health is degraded…` passes; `API health exposes details only…` fails on `health.runner.platform` being `undefined` (below) |
| same | test at `nice 10`, 3 runs | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| `app-progress-integration.test.mjs` (4 cases) | 42 busy loops ×3, `nice 10` ×3, `nice 19` ×2 | all green | all green |
| `research-package-http.test.ts` (29 cases) | 42 busy loops ×3 | all green | green in the loaded UT run above |

At `nice 19` the test process gets roughly 1/70 of a core. The authenticated `/health` deliberately bounds its Runner probe at 2 s (`settleWithin(runnerClient.health(), 2_000, undefined)` in `services/api/src/http/index.ts`) and answers without the Runner detail when that passes. That is a product bound, not a poll, and far past the 1.2–3.5× slowdown in the issue, so it is left alone.

Not reproduced here: CPU contention alone did not make the `app-progress-integration` or `research-package-http` cases fail on `40a50e010`; their waits read fixture data from disk, which CPU load does not slow the way the shared runners' I/O does. Their failing jobs are linked in the issue, and they pass under every load above.

Not in this change: the other inline loops of the same shape that the issue counts in files this change does not touch (its item 4). They can move to the helper when those files are next edited.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: the change is confined to test code, the test runner's preparation and one CI helper script. No product code, API, CLI or UI behaviour changes, so there is no user journey whose outcome could differ.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: none; UT/ST cases stop failing when the runner host is busy.
Compatibility and migration: none. The UT slice's preparation now downloads the research checks' evaluator checkout, Python 3.14 and wheels before any case runs (previously the same downloads happened inside the cases).

1554.author: yuanzhou75
1554.body:
﻿A copy whose package declared that it lost immutable evidence may still be continued, but it is not a complete copy: the receipt and the desktop Session now say which pieces are missing instead of staying silent.

The owner's decision on #1532 (comment `7236860015`) is what this implements, in his words: **继续研究不拦人，但必须明确降级** — the receipt and the place where a reader continues must name what is missing, not just count it, and nothing may present such a copy as complete.

## The two fields, and why there are two

`packages/schema/src/session.ts` gets two optional fields on `ResearchSnapshot`:

- `continuationAvailable` (unchanged) — "this copy **may** be continued";
- `continuationDowngraded` — "but it is **not a whole** copy";
- `missingImmutableEvidence` — the omissions that make it degraded, named one by one.

`continuationAvailable === true` therefore no longer implies completeness, and no surface may decide from that field alone. Both fields carry doc comments saying exactly that, because the pair is the whole contract.

## What actually changed in the restore path

`isFatalRestoreOmission` is untouched: it is still the definition of "this omission is missing immutable evidence".

What changed is that the omissions **the package itself declares** are no longer filtered away. Before, `restoreFailures` skipped anything the package already listed, so a copy whose package said "I lost `cas:…`" imported with `continuationAvailable: true`, no downgrade flag and nothing said anywhere. Now:

- `declaredImmutableMissing = imported.receipt.omissions.filter(isFatalRestoreOmission)` is taken **before** that filter;
- `restoreFailures` still only collects what **this import** produced, so a package's own declaration cannot fail the import;
- `continuationDowngraded = continuationAvailable && declaredImmutableMissing.length > 0`;
- both fields reach `result` (the HTTP receipt), `receipt.json` and the Session's `researchSnapshot`;
- the receipt's `omissions` is now `[...new Set([...imported.receipt.omissions, ...omissions])]`. It used to be overwritten by the import's own list, which made the receipt say **less** than the package it came from.

An export-side failure, `ENOSPC` and anything outside this path keep their existing statuses; this only changes how a declaration the package already made is presented.

## Desktop: the one surface, and why there is only one

The desktop import flow has no receipt screen. `apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx:764` is the evidence: on success it calls `setDialog(undefined)` and immediately `onOpen(result.importedSessionIds[0])`, so the dialog closes and the imported Session opens — what a reader sees next is that Session.

So the degraded state is stated where the reader decides: the read-only package panel on an imported snapshot (`ResearchPackage.tsx:245` derives the two fields, the banner renders beside the existing read-only line). It names every item of `missingImmutableEvidence` — long identifiers are listed in full and untruncated, per the owner's instruction — and the continue button stays enabled: allowed, but never silent.

Two surfaces are **not** in this PR: the web import receipt and the web continue entry. They need owner-confirmed frames of their own, and this PR has none for them; they follow in a separate PR that carries them together with their frames.

One layout fix came out of taking those frames, and belongs with this change: an omission is a machine identifier with no spaces, and it squeezed the panel's action button into a circle (`button` width collapsed from 78px to 53px). `apps/desktop/src/styles/research-package.css` now lets the list wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) and pins the button's own width.

## Frames

The owner looked at these frames before this PR was opened and asked for it as they are, including the instruction to keep the identifiers untruncated.
